<header>Sūtrasthāna-Ch. 19 (143)</header>

Remove the waste matter thoroughly and then have the patient sit. An adept physician should repeatedly extract the waste matter from the wounds caused by <term>kapha</term> <gloss>phlegm humor</gloss> and <term>vāyu</term> <gloss>wind humor</gloss>. 39. Press the wound from below and cause it to discharge in the direction of the hair growth, and align all deep connections <note>joints or deep tissue layers</note> and junctions properly. 40. In suturing the lips, proceed as previously described; the physician who understands joints should also apply the specified bandages for bone fractures, employing their own intelligence. 41. 

Uttiṣṭhano nipaṇṇasya śayanaṃ cāpi gacchataḥ || Gacchato vividhādyairnaiḥ nasya duṣyati sai vraṇaḥ || 42 || Sandhyasthikoṣṭhaprāptāśca śirā-snāyugatāstathau || Tathaivagāḍhagaṃbhīrāḥ sarvato viṣamasthitāḥ || Naite sādhayituṃ śakyā ṛte vandhairbhavanti hi || 43 || 

Thus ends the eighteenth chapter of the Sūtrasthāna in the Suśruta Saṃhitā. 18.

For a person who is rising, sitting, reclining, walking, or riding, the wound (once the proper bandage is applied) does not suffer pain. 42. Wounds located in the joints, bones, or viscera; wounds of the veins and tendons; dense and deep-seated wounds; and those that have become irregular on all sides cannot be treated effectively without the application of appropriate bandages. 43.

Thus ends the eighteenth chapter of the Suśruta Saṃhitā with the Hindi commentary by Pandit Muralidhara Sharma. 18.

### Nineteenth Chapter 19.

Now we shall explain the chapter regarding the care of the wounded <term>Vraṇitopāsanīyam</term> <gloss>rules for the care of the wounded</gloss>.

Here begins the explanation of the <term>Vraṇitopāsanīyam</term> <gloss>chapter on the regimen for the wounded</gloss>.

First, seek a suitable dwelling for the wounded patient; that dwelling should be constructed in an auspicious location. 1. In a house with a favorable site, clean, free from wind and sun, and protected from drafts, there will be no physical, traumatic, or mental diseases. 2. In that place, provide a bed that is uncrowded, well-spread, pleasant, with the head facing east, and accompanied by weapons <note>often for protection or religious warding</note>. 3. The wounded patient will have ease of movement and comfort on a well-spread bed. The gods dwell in the eastern direction, therefore the head should be placed toward the east. 4.

<note>(Verse 42) connected with the bandage.</note>

<summary>This page concludes the eighteenth chapter on surgical bandaging techniques and begins the nineteenth chapter concerning the proper environment and care for a wounded patient.</summary>
